cues.text: An Orphan of Noble Birth
Born in 1380 at Massa Marittima, a Sienese town governed by his father, Bernardine was orphaned by age six and raised carefully by pious aunts.
As a young man, he joined the Confraternity of Our Lady attached to a great Sienese hospital.
At twenty, he personally directed the hospital's care of plague victims during a severe outbreak, an experience of hands-on charity that shaped his later ministry.
Joining the Franciscans
Bernardine entered the Franciscan Order in 1402 and, after ordination, spent roughly a decade in relative obscurity and quiet preparation.
Around 1417, he began the extraordinary public preaching career that would make him, in the Catholic Encyclopedia's own assessment, 'the greatest preacher of his day.'
Apostle of the Holy Name
Bernardine became famous above all for his ardent promotion of devotion to the Holy Name of Jesus .
He popularized the now-familiar monogram IHS — the first three Greek letters of Jesus's name — displayed on a blazing sun.
He encouraged its display in homes and public buildings across Italy as a devotional replacement for superstitious symbols.
These included divisive factional emblems, such as those of the warring Guelph and Ghibelline parties, that still marked much of Italian public life.
Bonfires of Vanity and Public Reform
Preaching often in the vernacular rather than Latin so that ordinary people could follow him directly, Bernardine denounced gambling, usury, and immorality with famous vigor.
At times, he gathered dice, cards, and other implements of vice from his listeners to be burned publicly in the town square.
This practice of dramatic public reform would later inspire Savonarola's own more famous 'bonfires of the vanities' decades afterward.
Accusations and Vindication
Bernardine's promotion of the IHS symbol drew suspicion from some quarters as a dangerous innovation, and he was formally accused of heresy on three separate occasions.
Each time, papal investigation — including a direct examination by Pope Martin V — fully vindicated his teaching and orthodoxy.
Martin even urged him afterward to preach in Rome itself.

Bernardine repeatedly declined offered bishoprics, including the see of his own native Siena, preferring to remain free for his itinerant preaching mission, remarking that all of Italy was already his diocese.
Legacy

As vicar general of the Observant Franciscans from 1438, Bernardine grew the reformed branch of the order from roughly 150 friars to over 4,000 within his own lifetime, reforming hundreds of convents along the way.
He died at Aquila in 1444 and was canonized within six years, honored ever since as the Apostle of the Holy Name and one of the towering preachers of the fifteenth-century Church.
